summary:
AgriGuard AI seems to be a platform that pulls from NASA POWER data to give farmers a better sense of local climate stuff. It shows things like temperature, rainfall and wind on dashboards so people can check conditions in specific spots. I think the idea is to cut down on some of the guesswork when climate keeps shifting and affecting crops.

The tools include looking at risks over time and comparing different strategies like crop rotations or what happened after past shocks. Users can explore trends and see where stresses might hit but it feels like some of the comparisons are still a bit hard to pin down right away. Making the data easier to use is probably the main point so decisions end up more informed.

Climate changes hit planning and farm choices pretty hard so access to this kind of info could help with resilience. I am not totally sure how all the parts connect yet but the historical analysis stands out as useful.
details:
## 1. What Does the Project Do and How Does It Work?

AgriGuard AI is an agricultural intelligence platform powered by NASA that enables farmers and farmers' decision makers to understand climate data and take better farming decisions.

Environment this site uses NASA POWER environmental data to show you location based mean, max/min temperature, relative humidity precipitation wind speed, and solar radiation.

Access a geographic location and date range to view environmental conditions in interactive dashboards, maps, charts, and historical data visualizations.

AgriGuard AI includes several key features:

• **Global Dashboard:** Brings location-specific environmental data through interactive maps and visualizations.

• **NASA Data Explorer:** enables users to investigate NASA POWER climate variables with historical observations.

• **Climate Risk Analysis:** Assesses environmental factors such as temperature stress and rainfall variability to detect possible climate-related risks affecting agriculture.

• Crop Rotation Advisor. Assists in comparing alternate crop rotation options based on the climate data that is supplied and documented agricultural literature.

• **Climate Shock Replay:** Allows users to explore historical climate variations and understand how past environmental events may affect agricultural planning.

• **Decision Regret Engine:** this engine evaluates the relative performance of several different alternative farm enterprise and management decisions in the same or similar climates.

## 2. What Are the Benefits?

AgriGuard AI simplifies intricate environment data. This is the core of its advantages:

• Offers climate data based on the location of the user.

• Assist users in picking up the gradual change in rainfall and temperature.

• Climate smart agriculture planning.

• Enables searching on historical climate data.

• Allows assessment of different crop rotation and farming practices.

• Promotes data-based decisions rather than relying on guesswork.

It is not intended to ensure crops, profits, or farms, but rather to inform decisions.

## 3. What Is the Intended Impact?

The effect AgriGuard AI aims to have AgriGuard AI is hoping to make agriculture more sustainable and resilient to climate change.

Climate variability uncertainty in what to plant and when to plant makes it difficult to plan for the farm year to year. AgriGuard AI packages NASA data to inform farmers of potential climate issues and to help them explore other options.

In the longer term, the project will help access to information on the environment, promote decisions based on sound information and support systems that are more resilient to future climate conditions.

## 4. Tools, Programming Languages, and Technologies

Our team built the platform on cutting-edge data-processing and web development tools.

**Frontend:**

• React.js

• Vite

• JavaScript

• Tailwind CSS / CSS

• Recharts for data visualization

• Interactive maps - Leaflet and React Leaflet.

• Lucide React for icons

**Backend:**

• Python

• FastAPI

• Pandas

• NumPy

**NASA Data Source:**

• NASA POWER API

**Development and Deployment:**

• Visual Studio Code

• Git and GitHub

• Vercel for frontend deployment

• Render for backend deployment

This application has a browser interface that can link to a Python backend that pulls NASA POWER data for display, store, and analysis.

## 5. What Makes the Project Creative?

The innovative element of AgriGuard AI is its unique integration of NASA environmental data and a suite of agricultural decision support tools in a single application.

Rather than just providing access to temperature and precipitation readings, the project links climate exploration to climate research, crop rotation comparison, and decision regret assessment.

The unique feature of the Decision Regret Engine is it considers ways others on the shortlist investigated across climate scenarios and the distance of the selected strategy from the best scoring alternative in each scenario.

On top of that, the interactive feature of Climate Shock Replay helps users better understand the history of environmental change and its significance for planning.

## 6. What Factors Did Our Team Consider?

During development, we considered:

• Why the need for dependable NASA environmental data.

• Climate variability that depends on the place.

• Climate conditions and date ranges of the past.

• Information on how much data is available and, which observations are missing.

• A demand for calculations that are clear and easy to understand.

• The constraints of relying solely on environmental data to forecast crop productivity.

• How easy and accessible it is for people who are tech-savvy and not very tech-savvy.

• Flexible design and useful for use on various devices.

• Why unfounded agricultural recommendations are to be avoided.

We want to differentiate between what has been observed, what data have been derived from calculations and how land has been interpreted so that users can make an informed link to the evidence.

**Mostly, AgriGuard AI takes NASA POWER environmental data and makes it an easy-to-use agricultural intelligence system, allowing its users to explore climate data, assess potential options, and move toward better and more climate-aware results.**
